clips.linkedin:
Your AI can sort last year's budget into what built memory and what prompted action.

In most B2B teams, below the line is the bulk of the budget. Trade shows, events, direct outreach, email. Above the line is often small or missing, and that's usually the gap. If nobody in the market has heard of you before your salesperson calls, every deal starts from cold.

So it's worth knowing your own split. Give your AI your spend by line item and it hands back a table classing each line as above the line, below the line or digital that could be either, with the job it was doing and the overall split. It marks anything it can't classify rather than guessing.

This is from our Basics episode on above and below the line, and the podcast voices are AI-generated. Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/above-the-line-below-the-line-basics/
clips.text: Does any of this apply in business-to-business marketing? It sounds very consumer. It applies, the mix just looks different. In most business-to-business teams, below the line is the bulk of the budget. Trade shows, events, direct outreach, email, the sales team's own materials. Above the line is often small or missing altogether, and that's usually the gap. If nobody in the market has heard of you before your salesperson calls, every deal starts from cold.

Your AI can sort last year's budget into what built memory and what prompted action.

Above the line builds memory. Below the line prompts action. Most teams have never checked how last year's money actually split between the two, and when the numbers are reviewed separately, the fast ones win every argument.

Give your AI your media and marketing spend by line item. It hands back a table classing each line as above the line, below the line or digital that could be either, with the job each was doing and the overall split. Anything it can't classify from the description, it marks rather than guessing.

The prompt is in the show notes.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/above-the-line-below-the-line-basics/
clips.text: Get AI on this: sorting last year's budget into memory and action. Give it your media and marketing spend by line item, and it hands back a table classing each line as above the line, below the line or digital that could be either, with what job it was doing, and the overall split. It'll mark anything it can't classify from the description rather than guessing. Second, get AI on checking whether a campaign is genuinely through the line. Give it the campaign plan and the assets for each channel, and it checks whether one idea runs through the broadcast pieces and the targeted ones, listing any channel where the message or look has drifted.
